name: Gilraen, Dúnedain Protector
oracle_text: {2}, {T}: Exile another target creature you control. You may return that card to the battlefield under its owner's control. If you don't, at the beginning of the next end step, return that card to the battlefield under its owner's control with a vigilance counter and a lifelink counter on it.
blocked_sentences: If you don't, at the beginning of the next end step, return that card to the battlefield under its owner's control with a vigilance counter and a lifelink counter on it.

needs.what: A way for `exile` to record which objects it moved under a name -- the `as` binding `sacrifice` and `reveal` already have -- so a later `delay` can return exactly those cards with `{"binding": "exiled"}`. "Return *that card*" from inside a delayed trigger has no expressible subject today.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `{"target": "t1"}` names the exiled card correctly during the ability's own resolution, but `turn.py`'s delayed-trigger runner builds its EffectContext with `targets={}`, so a `target` selector inside a `delay`'s effects resolves to nothing; `delay` carries only `bindings` and `source_oid`. `exile` writes no binding -- it takes `objects`, `until_leaves` and `playable_this_turn` and nothing else -- so there is no name for the delay to carry. The one reachable substitute, `{"zone": "exile", "exiled_with": "self"}`, requires setting `until_leaves` on an ability that is not an O-Ring effect and is source-scoped rather than resolution-scoped: it accumulates every card Gilraen ever exiled, so a second activation's "you may return that card" would drag back a card declined on an earlier activation. `snapshot` binds a dict of characteristics, not an object a `put_onto_battlefield` can move.
